pos.personaBrief: No verified possession evidence (gap); from general knowledge plus the verified Total Football model he copied from Michels (Brazil, 1977), he wanted his sides to control the ball rather than concede it.

pro.personaBrief: No verified progression evidence (gap); from general knowledge, his 'ponto futuro' idea of passing into the space a runner will reach made him value vertical, line-breaking passes over safe recycling, without fixing a touch count.

est.personaBrief: The verified Total Football model (Brazil, 1977) points to interchange and players leaving their zones, while his methodical, European-style coaching also demanded clearly rehearsed roles.

lar.personaBrief: No verified width evidence (gap); from general knowledge, he made 'overlapping' full-backs popular in Brazil, so width came from full-backs more than from fixed touchline wingers.

blo.personaBrief: No verified block evidence (gap); from general knowledge, and in line with the verified Michels-style Total Football project (1977), he wanted forwards pressing and the team defending high.

mar.personaBrief: No verified marking evidence (gap); from general knowledge, his Total Football inspiration and the Brazilian zonal tradition point to protecting spaces, though set pieces in that era were mostly man-marked.

pla.personaBrief: Verified: on taking charge of Brazil he 'tried to implement his own philosophy', modelled on Total Football (1977), so he put his own model ahead of the opponent.

res.personaBrief: The verified evidence covers only his philosophy; from general knowledge, his 1978 Brazil was criticised as pragmatic, and he called it the 'moral champion' after an unbeaten exit, valuing results and how the team was judged alike.

sis.personaBrief: Verified: he imposed his own Total Football system on Brazil (1977); from general knowledge, he tied stars to tactical roles and was criticised for putting the system ahead of Brazilian individual flair.

jog.personaBrief: No verified player-profile evidence (gap); from general knowledge, as a military physical trainer (Cooper test) he put physical conditioning at the centre and wanted midfielders who ran.

bas.personaBrief: No verified squad-building evidence (gap); from general knowledge, his Flamengo (1978-80) was built on the club's own academy generation (Zico, Júnior, Leandro, Adílio, Andrade, Tita).

lid.personaBrief: No verified people-management evidence (gap); from general knowledge, he was an army captain with a strict, top-down style, consistent with the verified fact that he 'took command' and imposed his philosophy (1977).
